tasks.short: Record animal genealogy, feeding, appearance, behavior or breeding.

steps.what: Read the posted feeding line for this animal.
Record genealogy, appearance, behavior and breeding.

tasks.design: The veterinary assistant still watches the animal and writes genealogy, appearance, behavior and breeding by hand into the existing record. A feeding line is already posted in the {DOCS}, with animal, feed, amount, time and the poster's name, so the hunt for the paper card is shorter. Nothing sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: The feeding card sat on paper, so the assistant hunted it before writing what they saw.
tasks.enabler_now: The practice file already holds a feeding line. Showing animal, feed, amount, time and the poster's name is configuration of that file.
tasks.still_hard: Appearance, behavior and breeding are what the assistant sees in the cage. A feeding line does not see them.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant notices a change in the animal that a posted line does not carry.
tasks.altitude: The week is still the animals. Less time goes to hunting a feeding card. The assistant still records what they see.

reach.task: Post the feeding line before the round.
reach.learn: The line needs animal, feed, amount, time and the poster's name, or the assistant reads the paper card.

reach.task: Read the assistant's record when called.
reach.learn: The assistant's record is what they saw. It is not a diagnosis.

reach.task: Use the breeding note in the study file.
reach.learn: The scientist does not replace the assistant's observation.

evidence.claim: Watching the animal and writing genealogy, appearance, behavior and breeding stays with the assistant. A posted feeding line can be a shorter read. The record itself is not shorter. Model knowledge.
A preprint found verified errors in 31.3% of 565 notes from three scribes. This design drafts no animal note.
Health data of a person are a special category. An animal feeding line is not a person's health record. This design adds no store of a person's health.
Using logs of staff needs works-council consent. This design does not log the assistant and does not record the round.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: this task is the assistant's own record of one animal on the round. Client advice, the research report and the bill sit outside it. The veterinary technician posts the feeding line before the round.

Structured input: one feeding line in the {DOCS} with animal, feed, amount, time and the poster's name. If the line is missing or free text, the assistant reads the paper card and that read is not shorter.

The assistant still writes the record by hand. Nothing sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet. There is no commit, so there is no gate on a sent version. Writing the record is internal, not a send outside the organisation.

A model is not used. The prior that a model is needed is refused: the assistant has to see the animal. The prior that the line is special-category health data is refused: it is an animal's feed, not a person's health. Existing system runtime is not the assistant's time.
unknowns: Whether this clinic's feeding line already has animal, feed, amount, time and a name, or only a paper card.
Whether national rules set a retention period for animal records. The human medical dossier period is not assumed here.
research_questions: Who posts the feeding line, the veterinary technician or the veterinarian?
What share of rounds start with no line the assistant can read?

already_counted.description: Reading a missing or free-text feeding card by hand, inside the remaining read.

incremental.description: Checking that the feeding line still has animal, feed, amount, time and a poster's name.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the feeding line is often missing or free text, so the assistant still hunts the paper card and the read is not shorter. High: most lines carry animal, feed, amount, time and a name, and only that hunt shrinks. Watching the animal and writing the record stay. The high stays under the net after the field check.

tasks.still_hard: The client asks about this animal, today. The answer is the conversation, not the diet line.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant hears what the client will not accept from a sheet, and answers in the room.

tasks.short: Write reports and maintain research information.

Write reports and maintain the research information.

tasks.still_hard: What belongs in the report is what the assistant saw on the study. A posted line does not write it.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant chooses what the day's observation means for the study record.
tasks.altitude: The week is still the bench. Less time goes to hunting a study note. The assistant still writes the report.

reach.task: Post the research line before the report is written.
reach.learn: The line needs study, animal, observation, date and the author's name, or the assistant reads the paper note.

reach.task: Confirm the animal named on the study line.

reach.task: Read the report when the study needs a clinical view.
reach.learn: The report is the assistant's observation, not a diagnosis.

tasks.short: Keep the book, bill customers and count inventory.

steps.what: Read the posted price for this service.
Perform bookkeeping, billing customers and the inventory count.

tasks.design: The veterinary assistant still keeps the book, hands the bill to the customer in the clinic, and counts the inventory. A price is already posted in the {DOCS}, with service, price, date and the poster's name, so the hunt for the paper price is shorter. Nothing sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: The price sat on a paper list, so the assistant hunted it before writing the book or handing the bill.
tasks.enabler_now: The practice file already holds a price line. Showing service, price, date and the poster's name is configuration of that file.
tasks.still_hard: The count is physical, and the bill is handed to the customer in the room. A price line does not do either.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant sees what was used, what is left on the shelf, and what the customer is charged for today.
tasks.altitude: The week is still the book, the counter and the shelf. Less time goes to hunting a price. The assistant still writes the book, hands the bill and counts.

reach.task: Post the price before the book is written.
reach.learn: The line needs service, price, date and the poster's name, or the assistant reads the paper list.

reach.task: Take the bill at the counter.
reach.learn: The bill is handed over in the clinic. It is not sent on.

reach.task: Name the service that was done.
reach.learn: The veterinarian does not keep the assistant's book.

evidence.claim: The book, the bill handed over in the clinic, and the inventory count stay with the assistant. A posted price can be a shorter read. The book, the handover and the count are not shorter. Model knowledge.
A preprint found verified errors in 31.3% of 565 notes from three scribes. This design does not draft the bill.
Health data of a person are a special category. A price and a bill are not a person's health record.
A decision about a person may not rest solely on automated processing. This design does not decide the bill by automation.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: this task is the assistant's own book, the bill they hand over at the counter, and the inventory count. The animal record, the client advice and the research report sit outside it. The practice clerk posts the price before the book is written.
Structured input: one price line in the {DOCS} with service, price, date and the poster's name. If the line is missing or free text, the assistant reads the paper list and that read is not shorter.

The assistant still writes the book, hands the bill to the customer in the clinic, and counts the shelf. Nothing sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet. There is no commit, so there is no gate on a sent version. The prior that billing is an outside act is refused: handing the bill at the counter is not a send outside the organisation.

A model is not used. The prior that standard software already does this book is not a saving: the assistant still writes it. The prior that a person must approve a sent version is refused: nothing is sent. Existing system runtime is not the assistant's time.
unknowns: Whether this clinic's price line already has service, price, date and a name, or only a paper list.
Whether some bills leave later by post. That later sending is outside this task and is not designed here.
research_questions: Who posts the price, the practice clerk or the veterinarian?
What share of bills are handed over at the counter, rather than prepared for a later posting?

incremental.description: Checking that the price line still has service, price, date and a poster's name.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the price is often missing or free text, so the assistant still hunts the paper list and the read is not shorter. High: most lines carry service, price, date and a name, and only that hunt shrinks. The book, the bill handed over, and the count stay. The high stays under the net after the field check.
